he legal field is witnessing rapid changes with the emergence of
technology, changing methods of legal service delivery and
increasing demands for efficient and accessible legal solutions.
These developments create a need for innovative approaches to
address contemporary challenges in the legal ecosystem. With the
objective of encouraging innovation and entrepreneurial thinking in
the field of law, the School of Law, Forensic Justice, & Policy Studies,
National Forensic Sciences University, Delhi Campus, is organising
the National Legal Hackathon, 2026.
The competition aims to provide a platform for students and young
innovators to identify existing problems in the legal ecosystem and
present their ideas, initiatives or existing startups developed to
address such problems. The competition encourages participants to
think beyond conventional methods and develop solutions having
practical application and potential for wider implementation.
The competition will provide an opportunity to present innovative
ideas before a panel of experts and receive recognition for solutions
demonstrating originality, relevance and practical potential.

Guidelines
The competition is open to students/PHD scholars of universities
and colleges across India.
Participation shall be allowed only in teams. Each team shall
consist of a minimum of two (2) and a maximum of four (4)
members.
A participant shall be a member of only one team.
Teams may comprise participants from the same or different
institutions.
A complimentary workshop on “Legal Startups” shall be
conducted on 16th October 2026. Teams may attend the
workshop to gain insights into legal innovation and startup
development. Participation in the workshop is optional.
The proposed startup/innovation or existing startup/initiative
must pertain to the legal field and should address a problem,
need, gap or challenge arising within the legal ecosystem,
including those faced by lawyers, law firms, law students, legal
professionals, clients, legal institutions or other stakeholders in
the delivery, practice, study or administration of law.
Each team shall be permitted to present one startup/innovation
idea or initiative only.
The competition shall be conducted in three stages. Teams
shall first submit their proposal through the prescribed online
submission process.
Based on the submissions received, 20 teams shall be
shortlisted for the In-Campus Round.

competition, preliminary and final. The preliminary round will
be conducted on Friday, October 16, 2026, and the Final on
Saturday, October 17, 2026. The top 5 teams will proceed to the
final round. The Finals shall be adjudged on the basis of
research undertaken, steps of implementation, methods
adopted for improvisation, application success, Novelty as
parameters, and presentation. The teams will be adjudged
according to these parameters.

4) SOLD!
SOLD is not your typical math event. It’s a high-level strategy and
negotiation challenge where every move counts. Teams of three will
step into a game of bidding, trading, and outsmarting rivals. The real
twist? It’s not about solving problems. The spotlight is on the auction
floor and trading table, where your negotiation skills and resource
management decide your fate. In the end, victory belongs to the team
that finishes with the largest virtual funds.
ROUND INFORMATION
Introduction Round
The event begins by assigning placards to the teams, going over the
rules and flow of the event, and introducing the event volunteers
and their roles in the event. Every team is given the same amount
of virtual funds ( or credits ) to begin with.
Auction Round
The event’s auction round will be following a first-price sealed-bid
auction, and what will be auctioned off here? Equations! You can
acquire these equations in exchange for your credits through the
auction.In a first-price sealed-bid auction, each bidder submits a
sealed bid to the seller (that is hidden from other bidders). The
high bidder wins and pays his bid for the good.
When all the equations in the pool are auctioned off, the auction
round will have come to an end.
EVENT DESCRIPTION

Trade Round
Now that teams have acquired their equations, the floor is open for some
chaos! Each team is given a unique set of questions to solve. Once they
solve a question, they may submit the solution to the examiner, who
upon correction will award the respective team with credits, but there is
one extra requirement here. The examiner will also check for if the
required equation for the problem is in possession of the team
submitting the solution at the time or not.
But what if the team did not bid for that equation during the auction
round? It is very probable for that to be the case since questions are only
distributed after the auction round. Hence the trade round.You can trade
equations for credits among other teams. Both teams involved in the
trade will head to the registrar where the trade will be officiated.
This round will end after a certain stipulated amount of time. Once the
trading round ends, the event will be officially declared over.
